_doc: Per-rule false-positive budgets for detections/score_benign.py. A rule not listed uses `default`: enforce at 0 hits, so a new rule must stay silent on the benign corpus or a human approves a budget for it. mode `enforce`: an overrun fails CI (score_benign.py --enforce). mode `shadow`: an overrun is only a CI warning (for a rule a human accepts while its corpus is not yet trusted; no entry uses it today). `max_hits` is the most benign hits the rule may raise over the whole committed corpus for its logsource: set it to the most hits over the committed seed and ten reseeds of every synthetic slice (`score_benign.py --reseeds 10`, the 'most' column), not one seed's count, so a routine version bump of a slice does not trip it. Optional `max_rate_per_10k` caps the rate. Every entry needs a `why` that starts 'documented noise:' (a deliberately generic or hunting rule, or a falsepositives class the rule names) or 'rule defect, tracked in detections/RULE_DEFECTS.md <ID>:' (an entry of that tracker); score_benign.py fails any other. Raising a budget, or moving a rule to shadow, is a human decision: this file is a protected path that needs a human approval before merge. `unscored` maps a rule that no benign slice reads (no slice with its product and service) to the reason; --check/--enforce fail for an unscored rule not listed there, and for a listed rule that is scored now.
